summary: The High Terraces: terraces above the clouds where the air is still and the sky is close, whose watchers write to the Mirror's keepers and never call what they see a prophecy.

cloud_warden.name: The Cloud-Warden
cloud_warden.desc: Ithrael is warden of the high terraces and keeper of the old star tables. He climbs the stairs at every dusk to see what the sky has done.

heavens_peace.name: Heaven Keeps Its Peace
heavens_peace.desc: The terraces are high, the air is thin and the stairs are many. Few have climbed them with anything but pilgrimage in mind, and Heaven has kept its peace.

storm_readers_spirit.name: The Storm-Readers
storm_readers_spirit.desc: The storm-readers watch the weather over the whole south-west from towers cut into the rock. They see a gale a day before the coast does, and say so.

long_sight.name: The Long Sight
long_sight.desc: The watchers of Heaven keep records of the sky for longer than any court has kept its accounts. What they see is written down plainly, and is read plainly, and nothing more is claimed.

heaven_welcomes.name: Heaven Welcomes All
heaven_welcomes.desc: Pilgrims of every realm and kind climb the stairs of Heaven for the view and the quiet. They are fed, housed and sent down again, and none is asked their name.

omens_in_the_sky.title: Omens in the Sky
omens_in_the_sky.desc: The watchers see a long-tailed star and storms that do not move. They write that it is a sign of weather, not of fate, and ask whether the tables should go to Gala or stay in the hall.

focuses.name: The High Terraces
focuses.desc: Heaven is one high state: terraces above the clouds where the air is still and the sky is close. Its Cloud-Warden, Ithrael, keeps the old tables of the stars and the weather over the south-west.

focuses.name: The Cloud-Warden
focuses.desc: Ithrael is the warden of the high terraces and the keeper of the star tables. He wears a grey cloak the colour of the morning mist.

focuses.name: Terraces Above the Clouds
focuses.desc: Terraces cling to the cliff above the cloud-line, planted with barley, tea and bitter herbs. The farmers work them roped to iron rings.

focuses.name: The Warden's Hall
focuses.desc: The warden's hall is a round room of grey stone with a roof open to the sky. Its council sits on benches ringed round a pool, and watches the stars in the water.

focuses.name: The Still Air
focuses.desc: The air above the clouds is still, and a lamp burns without flickering. Quarrels seem to lose their edge up here, and councillors speak slowly.

focuses.name: Heaven Keeps Its Peace
focuses.desc: Heaven wants nothing but its stairs, its tables and its view. It sends word to every court that it will keep its peace, and asks only the same.

focuses.name: Watchers of the Sky
focuses.desc: Observation towers rise on the highest ridges, each with a brass ring, a slate and a keeper. The watchers sleep by day and write by night.

focuses.name: The Star Tables
focuses.desc: The star tables are copied out afresh on fine vellum, with the old errors corrected in red. Copies go to every Sunhot court that asks.

focuses.name: The Storm-Readers
focuses.desc: A school of storm-readers is founded in the lower tower, learning to tell a gale from a squall by the colour of the cloud-bank. Their forecasts are posted on the stairs.

focuses.name: Omens in the Sky
focuses.desc: Something strange is seen in the sky, and the watchers write it down without comment. They ask the warden what is to be done with such a record.

focuses.name: Letters to the Mirror's Keepers
focuses.desc: The watchers write to the keepers of the Mirror of First Rain at Gala, with their records of the sky. The Mirror's keepers answer with thanks and a question.

focuses.name: The Long Sight
focuses.desc: Records of the sky are kept for generation after generation, each in a numbered chest. What they show is read plainly, and nothing more is claimed for it.

focuses.name: What the Sky Cannot Show
focuses.desc: The watchers write a short rule on the door of the hall: no sign may be called a prophecy. They have seen what fear does to those who are told their end.

effects.tooltip: A sign read as a certainty can frighten people into the deeds it foretells.

focuses.name: Pilgrims to Heaven
focuses.desc: Pilgrims climb the stairs of Heaven for the view and the quiet, in lines that stretch down the mountain. They are fed, housed and sent down again.

focuses.name: The Pilgrim Stairs
focuses.desc: The stairs are recut in the living rock, with a handrail of rope and a rest-shelf at every hundred steps. A fit pilgrim climbs them in a day.

focuses.name: Houses for Pilgrims
focuses.desc: Stone rest-houses with hearths and bedrolls are built beside the stair, kept by the terrace families in turn. Pilgrims leave a coin or a verse.

focuses.name: Heaven Welcomes All
focuses.desc: Any pilgrim may climb, and any may leave. The warden asks only that they take nothing and leave no mark, and they do as he asks.
